title: Sharp Tie-Point Interval Length for Optimal Value via Within-Cell Outcome Collisions
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; no in-scope route to field after post-repair math and decision panels passed.
gap_reasons: Its sharpness is nevertheless confined to the exact tie in a highly structured local experiment with uniform known cell masses, balanced known treatment assignment, Bernoulli outcomes, and bounded local magnitudes.

The heterogeneous extension establishes uniform asymptotic coverage and the same null length constant, but it does not characterize pointwise heterogeneous optimal length, and its exact conditional calibration applies only to the common-magnitude submodel.
paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved the compact sign-mixture experiment, the all-procedure sharp tie-point expected-length lower bound, and attaining observable intervals; it also proved a bounded heterogeneous-class coverage and tie-length extension. After a known-design-constant repair and named closest-work comparisons, fresh D0.5 math and decision panels passed with no findings. The field claim fell to subfield because sharpness remains tied to a narrow local design and exact tie, while pointwise heterogeneous optimal length and exact heterogeneous calibration remain open.
tldr: For the common-magnitude class, within-cell outcome collisions yield the compact Gaussian experiment \(W\sim N(h^2/\sqrt2,1)\), the sharp tie-point expected-length constant \(C_{\alpha,H}=\int_0^H\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-t^2/\sqrt2)dt\), and both Gaussian and exact folded-binomial attaining intervals. For freely heterogeneous bounded cell magnitudes, the collision shift is the quadratic average \(m_{2,d}\), whereas the causal value increment is the first average \(m_{1,d}\). An outer-uniform central limit theorem over deterministic magnitude arrays, together with \(m_{1,d}^2\le m_{2,d}\), makes the same observable Gaussian collision interval uniformly valid over all magnitude vectors and signs; constant-magnitude diagonals are asymptotically least favorable. The diagonal restriction lower bound then gives the same sharp expected-length constant at the exact tie. The theorem does not assert an occupancy-adaptive conditional supremum, the pointwise heterogeneous expected-length frontier, or exact heterogeneous calibration.
gap: The global discrete optimal-value result gives a mean-squared-error rate but explicitly does not provide uniform confidence intervals. Paninski supplies paired perturbations and the collision scale, Pratt supplies the expected-length identity, and Kipnis supplies related fixed-total sharp-testing machinery; none gives the causal compact experiment, all-sign honest length constant, or attaining interval. Existing optimal-value inference does not uniformly cover positive gap atoms that approach zero while their cells retain bounded occupancy.
fill: The compact likelihood limit identifies the exact local information, the Neyman--Pearson envelope gives the all-procedure tie-point length lower bound, and two collision intervals attain it. The Gaussian interval is defined measurably by a full anchored interval on the zero-collision event, and the folded-binomial interval has exact conditional finite-sample coverage.
